No direct call site in frontend/src (grep for bcrypt/tweetnacl/nacl over frontend/src: zero hits). The build ships the algorithm; use is the question a finding answers.

Dev-only tree, but committed in the lockfile and installed with the build. No application call site (grep over frontend/src: zero).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: `uncleHash != uncle.Hash` — compares the block-header's uncle hash list entry against a digest re-fetched via eth_getUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex, as a consistency check on data from the operator's own geth node. Real non-constant-time digest comparison, but both operands are public blockchain data with no secret on either side, so there is no secret-dependent timing channel to exploit; the mismatch aborts the aggregation with an error. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl provides Ed25519 signatures (plus X25519 ECDH and XSalsa20-Poly1305 — separate roster objects). Dep of sshpk (line 18080 `"tweetnacl": "~0.14.0"` inside sshpk's entry; also required by bcrypt-pbkdf at 6893), reachable via devDep request → http-signature → sshpk. No direct use in frontend/src. Shipped capability; Ed25519 signatures are Shor-vulnerable (migration ML-DSA-65) if ever exercised.

Quantum posture is fixed by the Ethereum protocol itself (Keccak-256 is pinned network-wide); not migration-relevant for an app-level inventory. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @ethersproject/pbkdf2 ^5.5.0 — PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, used by ethers for Web3 Secret Storage v3 keystore key derivation. This app (watchtheburn.com, read-only Ethereum burn analytics) never opens or creates keystores, but the package ships in the build tree. A KDF, not itself Shor-relevant; the exposure of an encrypted keystore is via its output cipher (AES-CTR via aes-js, reported separately).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The import at client.go:4 is used at client.go:71 — rand.Int(rand.Reader, 2^130-1) — "Generate cryptographically strong pseudo-random between 0 - max" for WebSocket JSON-RPC subscription IDs, so subscription IDs cannot be guessed/enumerated by clients. Go's crypto/rand is a CSPRNG (ChaCha20-based in Go 1.6+): correct tool, correct use, quantum-safe. Changeable here if ever needed.
